test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 17 Aug, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

An old man whom / we met while coming back / from our college lives / at my uncle’s place.
solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1' 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence is related to the use of the relative pronoun "whom."
 
• "Whom" is used as the object of a verb or preposition, but in this sentence, the requirement is for a subject pronoun due to the absence of a preposition directly before it.
 
• The correct pronoun to be used in this context is "who" because it serves as the subject of the verb "lives."
 
• Therefore, the sentence should correctly be "An old man who we met while coming back from our college lives at my uncle's place."

Hence, the correct answer is Option 1.

Correct sentence: *"An old man who we met while coming back from our college lives at my uncle's place."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The segments "we met while coming back" and "from our college lives" do not contain any grammatical errors and correctly use verbs and prepositions to describe the situation.
 
• "At my uncle’s place" correctly indicates the location where the old man lives, using the preposition "at" to specify a place.
 
• The error solely lies in the incorrect use of the relative pronoun "whom" instead of "who," which is a common mistake when distinguishing between subjects and objects in a sentence.
